records.name: Stormhold
records.held_by: The Vicecanons of Stormhold (the office the city invented); the Hist tree in the town square
records.summary: The province's northern gate and one of its eight great cities: a stone-and-mud city on mounds and ravines beside the river that marks the Morrowind border, built over the Ayleid ruin of Silyanorn around a waterfall. In 4E 201 it is run by Vicecanons and holds the state's customs, its frontier offices and the province's largest and oldest Dunmer minority.

notes.text: The city of the Valley of Storms region and the likeliest first sight of the province for a newcomer. (full TEXT: "Stormhold is the largest settlement of Shadowfen, a major city of Black Marsh, sited near the banks of the river that forms the border with Morrowind. The city of the Valley of Storms region and the likeliest first sight of the province for a newcomer.")

Barsaebic Ayleids founded Silyanorn here after 1E 198; the Hist later conquered them, by legend. The Dunmer used the site as the foothold of their slave trade, adding stone roads, light posts and bridges, and the city invented the Vicecanon office to try slavers. It was the Pact's capital of Black Marsh in 2E, held a prison under Warden Quintus Varus in the late 3E, and was overrun but lightly damaged by Umbriel's undead in 4E 48.

The waterfall, the ravine-severed mounds, the Hist in its pond and the Silyanorn substructure all survived 4E 48. The rest has been rebuilt in the 153 years since. The damage that remains is in the population. The Vicecanons keep the river customs and the frontier screen's offices here.

Argonians beside the largest and oldest Dunmer minority in Argonia, descended from a colonial population, about a fifth of the city. The western quarter was where the Argonians who worked for the Dunmer lived, and the memory is still live. Outsiders are met with pragmatism: this is the city that has always had to live with them. Several Vicecanons sit at once, one for each people.

River traffic to Morrowind and to Alten Corimont down the northern trunk road, the customs on that traffic, and the Stormhold Crystals dug in the tunnels below. Sedge mats, dried fish and reed goods arrive daily from Jal-Veesa and the weirs; the guild halls sit in the repurposed Ayleid compound.

The Hist tree stands in the town square in the middle of a pond, ringed by ancient pillars and a low stone wall, public and defended. Dunmer households keep their ancestors and a quiet Tribunal-shaped habit; the grave-stake tradition of the Argonians and the Ayleid-compound mortuary sit side by side.

A city on a mountainside: Dunmer ornate stone, stone roads, light posts and long wooden bridges over ravines, with large Argonian mud huts on the mounds between, and a waterfall running down through the old Ayleid compound.

D0 inside the walls, where guards keep order. Outside the gate are crocodile-infested ravines and sunken marsh; below the city the Silyanorn tunnels and a sunken Ayleid ruin are an outlaws' refuge (D3).

The Silyanorn undercity holds crystal tunnels and a lost book of wisdom about the natural energies of Black Marsh. The Conclave of Baal keeps its Vaults of Gemin. The old quarrel between the Argonian west quarter and the Dunmer is a further hook, and so are the Vicecanons' courts.

notes.text: Slough Point was an Imperial census-and-excise post with a Commission-built white bridge over a black tidal river, its guards chewed by fleshflies. UESP's Blackwood page lists it as an Imperial town in Blackwood, close to the Black Marsh border; the map puts it inside Black Marsh, beside Fort Rustmoth, which is how we place it. UESP has no page of its own.
The Empire built the post, bridge and customs house to tax the Blackwood Road. The Legion left and Imperial presence ends in canon by 4E 48; the families who served the post stayed on.

A village around the old customs house and the bridge. The tide still swamps the bridge for days at a time and shuts the crossing, as the Argonian Account describes. The toll is kept by the garrison of Fort Rustmoth next door.

The register places the Third Empire's Fort Swampmoth on the same road between Slough Point and Gideon; Rustmoth fits that placement and may be its map name, which we leave open.
Built by the Third Empire to command the Blackwood Road; rumoured emptied when the Legions were recalled at the Oblivion Crisis; not Imperial after 4E 48.
Held, but not by the Empire: an Archwarden garrison charges tolls and keeps a customs ledger for the successor state, in the old Imperial style.
Argonian soldiers under an old Archein-lineage captain; clerks; a few Nibenese families in the kitchens.
Tolls on the Blackwood Road, a levy on goods bound for Gideon and Leyawiin, and fines on smugglers.
No Hist: Imperial foundation. The garrison hatch and bury at village trees.
A square stone keep with corner towers and a yard, the Imperial eagle over the gate, a moat that is now a reed pond.
D1: a guarded fort; wildlife and fleshflies outside.
A captain who has been paid not to look at a cart; a ledger that does not agree with the barracks' stores.

records.name: Gemin
records.held_by: Wild; haunted; no one holds it
records.summary: The partially flooded, monster-infested ruin of the Conclave of Baal's vaults, north-west of Stormhold, where the tablet that finds Murkwood was kept.

notes.text: UESP's Vaults of Gemin are a ruined structure in Stormhold's city-state that once belonged to the Conclave of Baal, kept the ancient tablet for deciphering the Elder Scrolls and divining Murkwood's place, and sank into the ground when a spell failed.
The vaults sank when an associate of the Conclave cast a powerful spell. In the Simulacrum the Eternal Champion was sent in to recover the tablet.
A sunk, half-flooded ruin; the Conclave of Baal still sits in Stormhold and still cannot locate Murkwood without the tablet.
None live here; the Conclave pays treasure-seekers.
Once the Conclave's vault; now a source of tablet fragments and relics for scavengers and the Conclave's agents.
The Conclave's faith in learning and Molag Bal's name in their title; the Veesa-Teeleel call the ground sick.
A collapsed stone vault entrance in a slope of reeds; half-sunk columns, flooded halls and rune-marked walls.
D4: undead and monsters in flooded halls; the roof is unsafe.
The tablet itself; a Conclave scholar who needs someone to find the lower archive.

records.name: Loriasel
records.held_by: Wild; lamias and keystone-haunted undead
records.summary: A Barsaebic Ayleid citadel and amphitheatre on a hill over the Venomous Fens, its keystones and its lamia-infested caverns beneath.

notes.text: Loriasel is a ruined Ayleid citadel and amphitheatre built by the Barsaebics for the Ten Ancestors on a hill over the Venomous Fens.

Built after 1E 198 over subjugated Argonians. The Liege Lord bound his knights; the Enchanter turned the binding on him and had the knights kill him. In 2E 582 Dominion soldiers, lamia and ancient Ayleid warriors held it.

The ghost-knights were freed in 2E 582; the Enchanter's works and the keystones remain. Argonians put the amphitheatre to uses that the Ayleids never envisioned. The Veesa-Teeleel guard the ruin from looters.
None live here; lamias and undead; a guarded visitor's track from Jal-Veesa.
Once the Ayleid cult centre and keystone workshop; now a source of Ayleid relics, keystone shards and tombs for scavengers.
The Ten Ancestors; a shrine to Azura stands outside; Argonians remember the keystones as a theft of their dead.
A hilltop amphitheatre with a ring of ruined seats, an inner bailey and tomb wings below; pale stone and dead trees.
D4: lamias, undead knights and keystone-fed wards.
A keystone that still holds a soul; the Azura shrine outside and its keeper; a looter band missing since the monsoon.

the lamia caverns below open into the hill

notes.text: Gandranen is a Barsaebic Ayleid ruin in Shadowfen: a library of magical halls that draws books from any time, and a Fenlord's tomb crawling with undead slave-guardians.
Built by a sorceress of Hermaeus Mora to attract books; the halls drew in The Lusty Argonian Maid and Ruminations on the Elder Scrolls. Zahra entered about 2E 582 to find the Crown of Ascension.
The library still attracts volumes; its undead guards still serve the Fenlord.
None living; an occasional scholar.
Once a library and tomb; now a treasure for scholars and thieves.
Hermaeus Mora and the Fenlord's death-cult; the Veesa-Teeleel avoid it.
A half-sunk pale-stone ruin on a reed island among black water; shelf-lined halls in the dry part.
D4: Fenlord undead and the library's wards.
A book that should not exist in the library; the Fenlord's vault.

records.name: Mirasel
records.held_by: Wild; the Veesa-Teeleel keep watch from afar
records.summary: A small Barsaebic ayleid ruin on a sedge island east of Loriasel, with white arches in the reeds and a flooded undercroft.

notes.text: A Barsaebic Ayleid ruin marked on the map at (-8,-65); named by us in the Ayleid manner. UESP has no page (searched 2026-11-08).
Mirasel is a small Barsaebic Ayleid hall on a sedge island east of Loriasel, from the settlement that grew in the region after 1E 198. Nothing is recorded of it; its name is a map label.
The island is half-flooded and the Veesa-Teeleel of Reed-Sill Weir, a few cells to the north-east, will not go onto it and tell visitors it is sick ground.
Mirasel has no residents. Weir-wardens from Reed-Sill and Teel-Fen see its white arches on their rounds and have never seen a visitor stay.
It was a minor hall of the Ayleid settlement. Scavengers and relic-hunters now come from Jal-Veesa by the Teel-Fen creek.
A worn Ayleid altar sits under a vine on the island's crown, ringed by Veesa-Teeleel ward-stakes set facing in.
White arches stand in sedge with a fallen column lying across a black pool; the undercroft stairs go down into the water.
Giant snakes in the reeds and undead guardians below the arch. At D3 the stairs are drowned and the wardens do not cross to the island.
A Jal-Veesa relic-seller will pay for a rubbing of the altar, and a Teel-Fen warden says a ward-stake on the west side has been pulled.

records.name: Orimel
records.held_by: Wild; the Veesa-Teeleel keep watch from afar
records.summary: A small Barsaebic ayleid ruin on the high ground north-west of Slough Point (labelled [Outpost] on the map; reading it as a ruin), with white arches in the reeds and a flooded undercroft.

notes.text: The map labels Orimel [Outpost] at (-15,-69), north-west of Slough Point; we read it as a ruin and named it in the Ayleid manner. UESP has no page (searched 2026-11-08).

Orimel is a small Barsaebic Ayleid hall on high ground north-west of Slough Point, one of the settlements left by the Ayleids after 1E 198. The map labels it an outpost; we read it as a ruin. Nothing is recorded of it.
The mound is dry in the cool months and flooded in the wet; Vel-Sapha Stand's people watch it from the track and the Veesa-Teeleel call it sick ground.
Orimel has no residents. Hunters from Vel-Sapha Stand and the Fort Rustmoth garrison patrol the track below it. Neither side goes up.
It was a small Ayleid hall. Relic-hunters from Slough Point now come to it, with the odd Fort Rustmoth soldier looking for white stone.
A cracked Ayleid shrine-stone stands at the top of the mound with Veesa-Teeleel ward-stakes ringed at its foot, leaning in.
White arches rise from the reeds on the high ground, with vines over the fallen columns and black water in the lower rooms. The Rustmoth track runs below.
Undead guardians in the arch and snakes in the reed edge. At D3 the lower rooms are flooded and the track is the only safe place.
A Vel-Sapha hunter has a rubbing from the shrine-stone he cannot read, and a Fort Rustmoth sergeant wants the mound's ward-stakes counted.

records.name: Meliton
records.held_by: Wild; the Naka-Desh visit to hang chimes
records.summary: A dead Kothringi town of cairns and stone footings in the western hills, left empty since the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560.

notes.text: A Kothringi ruin on the map at (-14,-71); named by us in the style of Kothringi towns such as Korydon and Toklea. UESP has no page (searched 2026-11-08); the Kothringi do.

Meliton was a Kothringi town in the western hills that the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 left empty, part of a homeland that once held many such towns. Its Kothringi name is on the map; the dead were laid in the cairns outside it.
Cairns, footings and two standing walls on a hill-shoulder above Hutan-Aru, visited each year by the Naka-Desh who hang chimes in memory of their friends.
The ruin has no residents. The Naka-Desh come on foot from the west in the dry months, and Hutan-Aru hunters leave them alone.
Once a craft town of glass beads and moonstone. Treasure-diggers now work it, as do the Sul-Xan raiders who come for the cairns.
The Kothringi honoured Z'en, Dibella, Mara and Kynareth and their cairns still hold bead strings. Naka-Desh chimes hang in a single thorn tree beside the largest cairn.
Rings of stone footings on a hill, cairns heaped with glass beads and a chime-hung thorn tree at the centre. Hutan-Aru's smoke shows to the north.
Restless dead rise from the oldest cairns at night, and Sul-Xan diggers work the south side. At D3 the diggers are the greater danger by day.
A cairn with a humming doll the Naka-Desh will not discuss, and a Sul-Xan trench a Hutan-Aru elder wants filled.

notes.text: The map shows a Kothringi ruin at (-23,-76), close to the Cyrodiil border. We named it in the style of Kothringi towns such as Korydon and Toklea. UESP has no page (searched 2026-11-08).
Aithros was a Kothringi town in the far western hills, emptied by the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560 and never resettled. It lies a day south-west of Hutan-Veel, close to the Cyrodiil border.
Footings, cairns and a few walls above a stream, visited in the dry months by Naka-Desh chime-hangers from the border road.
The ruin has no residents. Naka-Desh come in small parties and Hixinoag villagers cut wood on the slope below without crossing it.
It was a craft town with beadwork and a pottery lane. Treasure-diggers and Cyrodilic relic-buyers from Nahk-Zeel Station now visit it.
The Kothringi's four powers are marked by four small cairns at the town's centre, each with a different colour of glass. Naka-Desh chimes hang from one tin frame.
Stone footings in a loose ring around four coloured cairns, with a tin chime-frame and a pottery heap by the stream. The border road is a day to the north.
Restless dead at the four cairns, and Sul-Xan raiders who dig from the stream side. At D3 the raiders come in the dark of the moon.
A pottery heap with unbroken Kothringi bowls that a Nahk-Zeel buyer pays well for, and a raider who left his tools in the trench.
